title: Grilled Escarole Toasts with Trout Roe
ingredients: ½ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
Eighteen ½-inch-thick baguette slices, cut on a wide diagonal
Crème fraîche and trout roe, for serving
method: Heat a grill. Swish the escarole heads, root end up, in a bowl of cold water to rinse out grit, then shake dry.
Whisk the ½ cup olive oil with thyme and garlic. Brush it over the escarole and season with salt and pepper.
Grill the escarole over moderate heat about 20 minutes, basting with the garlic oil now and then, until charred and tender.
Cool the escarole, chop it roughly and toss with any leftover garlic oil, salt and pepper.
Oil and season the bread slices and grill about 2 minutes, until marked on both sides.
Pile escarole on each toast, add a spoonful of crème fraîche and some trout roe.

title: Tuna Briks
ingredients: Two 7-oz. cans tuna packed in water, drained well and flaked
method: Gently mix the tuna, scallions, capers, parsley, olive oil and harissa; season with salt and pepper.
Make two stacks of three phyllo sheets and cut each stack across into four 4-by-12-inch strips; keep them under a damp towel.
Put a generous ¼ cup of filling at the near end of a strip and brush the far end with egg.
Fold the phyllo over the filling into a triangle and keep folding flag-style to the end; press to seal. Repeat.
Heat ¼ inch of canola oil in a cast-iron skillet until shimmering.
Fry four triangles at a time over moderately low heat, turning, 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Everything Twists
ingredients: One 14-oz. package all-butter puff pastry, thawed if frozen but still cold
method: Combine the three kinds of seeds with the dried onion, salt and garlic powder.
Line three baking sheets with parchment.
On a floured counter roll the pastry to 11 by 14 inches and halve it lengthwise.
Brush with egg wash, scatter the seed mix over, then slice crosswise into ¾-inch strips.
Twist each strip and set on the sheets 2 inches apart; freeze 30 minutes until firm.
Bake at 375° about 22 minutes until golden, rotating the sheets halfway. Cool about 10 minutes before serving.

title: Mexican Corn Popcorn
ingredients: ½ cup white cheese powder, such as King Arthur Vermont Cheese Powder
½ tsp. ground dried lime zest or 1 tsp. finely grated lime zest
method: Stir together the cheese powder, salt, chipotle powder, cilantro, lime zest and cayenne.
Put the oil and popcorn kernels in a large covered saucepan over moderately high heat.
Once popping starts, shake the pan regularly until it stops, 3 to 5 minutes.
Tip into a big bowl, toss with the melted butter, then toss with the cheese seasoning and serve.

title: Potato-Apple Pancakes
ingredients: 2 baking potatoes, peeled and grated on the large holes of a box grater
1 Granny Smith apple, peeled and grated on the large holes of a box grater
method: Wring out as much liquid as possible from the grated potato and apple.
Toss them in a bowl with the dill, flour, salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large nonstick skillet and add four ¼-cup mounds, pressing them flat.
Fry over moderately high heat about 2 minutes a side, adding another tablespoon of oil when you flip, until crisp and golden.
Drain briefly on paper towels and repeat with the rest. Serve with sour cream.

title: Roasted Fingerling Potato & Pressed Caviar Canapés
ingredients: 10 fingerling potatoes, scrubbed and halved lengthwise
Chives cut into twenty 1-inch lengths, for garnish
method: Heat the oven to 400°. Toss the potato halves with oil, salt and pepper on a rimmed sheet.
Roast cut side down about 25 minutes until tender and browned underneath; let cool to warm.
Roll the pressed caviar between plastic wrap into a 5-by-6-inch sheet about ⅛ inch thick and cut into 20 diamonds.
Turn the potatoes cut side up, add a dab of sour cream, a caviar diamond and a piece of chive. Serve at once.

title: Shrimp Cakes
ingredients: 1 lb. shelled and deveined shrimp, chopped
method: Stir the mayonnaise with the hot sauce for a dipping sauce.
Combine shrimp, panko, eggs, scallions, lemon zest, smoked paprika, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper.
Shape into eight cakes about ¾ inch thick.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and fry the cakes in batches over moderately high heat, about 4 minutes total, flipping once, until browned and cooked through.
Serve with the spicy mayo and lemon wedges.

title: Hand-Cut Fries with Smoked Aioli
ingredients: 1 tsp. pimentón de la Vera (smoked Spanish paprika)
1 Tbsp. plus 2 tsp. finely chopped flat-leaf parsley
3 large, very firm baking potatoes (about 2 lbs.), peeled and cut into ½-inch-thick sticks
method: Blend the mayo, garlic, smoked paprika and lemon juice in a food processor; stir in 2 tsp parsley, season and chill.
Rinse the potato sticks and dry them very well.
Heat 1 inch of oil to 250° and fry the potatoes in batches about 6 minutes, until nearly tender but pale. Drain.
Raise the oil to 350° and fry again in batches about 3 minutes until crisp and golden.
Drain, salt right away, sprinkle with the remaining parsley and serve with the aioli.

title: Provoleta with Oregano & Tomatoes
ingredients: One 1-inch-thick slice of provolone cheese (½ lb.)
method: Heat the oven to 450° and get a cast-iron skillet very hot on the stove.
Put in the provolone and sprinkle with half the oregano and half the pepper flakes.
Cook over moderate heat about 2 minutes until the underside browns, then flip and brown the other side about 2 minutes.
Scatter on the rest of the oregano and pepper flakes and the tomatoes.
Bake about 4 minutes until molten and the tomatoes are warm. Salt, add basil and serve with bread.

title: Spaghetti with Brussels Sprouts & Sausage
ingredients: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
½ lb. brussels sprouts, thinly sliced (about 3 cups)
method: Boil the spaghetti in salted water until al dente.
Meanwhile heat ¼ cup oil in a large nonstick skillet and cook the sprouts and sausage over moderately high heat about 5 minutes, until the meat is browned and cooked.
Add the panko and stir about 3 minutes until crunchy; add chives, salt and pepper.
Drain the pasta, spoon the sausage mixture over, drizzle with oil and serve with lemon.

title: Celery Root Bisque with Walnut-Parsley Gremolata
ingredients: 1 large leek, white and light green parts only, thinly sliced
2½ lbs. celery root, peeled and cut into 1-inch dice (8 cups)
One 2-inch chunk of Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese (1 oz.), plus ¼ cup freshly grated cheese
2 cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
method: Melt the butter in a large saucepan and soften the leek and garlic over moderate heat, about 5 minutes.
Add the celery root, the Parmesan chunk, the stock and 5 cups water; bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over moderately low heat about 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the celery root is soft.
While it cooks, toast the walnuts at 375° for 5 to 7 minutes, cool and chop finely.
Mix the walnuts with the olive oil, parsley and grated cheese for the gremolata.
Blend the soup in two batches until very smooth, return to a clean pot, add the cream, season and reheat.
Ladle into bowls and spoon gremolata on top.

title: Broccoli-Spinach Soup with Crispy Broccoli Florets & Croutons
ingredients: ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
2 cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
One 8-oz. baking potato, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
2 lbs. broccoli, stems peeled and sliced, florets cut into ½-inch pieces
4 oz. sourdough or ciabatta bread, cut into ½-inch dice
method: Heat the oven to 400°. In a big pot warm ¼ cup oil and cook the onion and garlic with salt and pepper 6 to 8 minutes, until soft and lightly browned.
Add 2 cups water, the stock, potato, broccoli stems and two-thirds of the florets; boil, then simmer about 30 minutes until everything is very soft.
Stir in the spinach just until it wilts.
Toss the leftover florets with 1 Tbsp oil and the bread cubes with the last 1 Tbsp oil; season both.
Roast the florets on half a sheet pan 10 minutes, then add the bread to the other half and roast about 10 minutes more until both are crisp.
Blend the soup in batches until silky, add the vinegar and season.
Serve topped with the crispy florets, croutons and chives.

title: Asparagus & Bok Choy Frittata
ingredients: 1 tsp. finely grated peeled fresh ginger
1 small head of bok choy (about ¾ lb.), cut into 1-inch pieces
¾ lb. asparagus, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
method: Heat the oven to 325°. Warm the vegetable oil in an ovenproof skillet and sizzle the scallions, ginger and garlic about 30 seconds.
Add the bok choy and cook about 2 minutes until wilted.
Add the asparagus and ½ tsp salt and cook about 3 minutes until nearly tender.
Spread the vegetables evenly, pour in the eggs with the pepper and remaining salt, and cook untouched about 2 minutes until the edge sets.
Bake about 25 minutes until firm, then drizzle with sesame oil and serve.

title: Cauliflower & Gruyère Soufflé
ingredients: ½ lb. cauliflower florets, cut into 1-inch pieces
6 oz. Gruyère cheese, shredded (2 lightly packed cups)
method: Boil the cauliflower in salted water about 7 minutes until very soft; drain, pat dry, mash and let it drain in a colander until cool.
Heat the oven to 350°. Butter a 6-cup soufflé dish with 1 Tbsp butter and set it on a rimmed sheet.
Melt the remaining butter, whisk in the flour and cook about 3 minutes until bubbling.
Slowly whisk in the milk, bring to a boil and simmer about 7 minutes, whisking, until thick. Season and let cool in a large bowl.
Stir in the cauliflower, then fold in the Gruyère and chives.
Whisk the eggs until foamy and fold them gently into the base.
Pour into the dish and bake about 1 hour 10 minutes until risen and browned. Serve immediately.

title: Oysters on the Half Shell with Spiced Cucumbers
ingredients: ¼ cup finely diced peeled Asian pear
¼ cup peeled, seeded and finely diced cucumber
12 freshly shucked oysters on the half shell, such as Rappahannocks
method: Toast the coriander seeds in a dry pan over moderate heat about 2 minutes, cool, then crack them in a mortar.
Stir the coriander together with the pear, cucumber, chile, cilantro, lime juice, ginger, fish sauce, oil, salt and pepper.
Set the oysters on a bed of crushed ice.
Spoon a little relish onto each and serve straight away with the extra relish alongside.

title: Spinach & Prosciutto Ravioli
ingredients: ½ lb. prosciutto, sliced ½ inch thick
1 stick plus 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into thin slices
4 oz. curly spinach, coarsely chopped (4 cups)
2 tsp. fennel pollen or ½ tsp. ground fennel
½ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
method: Dice the prosciutto and freeze about 30 minutes until very firm, then pulse in a food processor until finely chopped.
Blanch the 1 lb spinach about 1 minute, cool, squeeze completely dry and chop (about ½ cup).
Beat the ricotta smooth, then mix in the prosciutto, spinach, mascarpone, yolks and Parmesan; salt it and chill about 30 minutes.
For the dough, whisk the 00 flour and salt, add the 12 yolks and 1 Tbsp water to a well, and work into a shaggy dough with a fork.
Knead on a semolina-dusted surface about 5 minutes until smooth, wrap and rest 45 minutes.
Roll a quarter of the dough at a time through a pasta machine, twice on each of the first five settings, once on the sixth; halve and roll each half once on the thinnest.
Dot one sheet with two rows of eight teaspoon-size filling balls 1 inch apart, brush around them with water and cover with a second sheet.
Press out the air around each mound and cut with a 2-inch fluted cutter; keep on a semolina-dusted tray under a towel. You should get 64.
Boil the ravioli in two batches about 2 minutes until the edges are tender; save 1 cup cooking water.
In two skillets melt 4 Tbsp butter each with ¼ cup pasta water and half the chopped spinach; cook about 1 minute until wilted, then add half the ravioli to each and coat.
Move ravioli to a bowl; combine the pan juices in one skillet with the last 2 Tbsp butter, 1 tsp fennel pollen and ¼ cup cheese and swirl about 1 minute until slightly thickened.
Pour over the ravioli and finish with the remaining fennel pollen and cheese.

title: Extra-Crispy Fried Chicken
time: 1 hr 15 min active; 4 hr 30 min total
ingredients: ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. kosher salt
1½ Tbsp. minced rosemary, plus 4 medium sprigs
5 minced bay leaves, preferably fresh, plus 5 whole leaves
3 garlic cloves, minced, plus 1 head broken into cloves
1 Tbsp. hot sauce, such as Tabasco
Grapeseed or vegetable oil, for frying
method: Heat the oven to 200°. Mix 3 Tbsp kosher salt, 2 Tbsp pepper, the olive oil and the minced herbs, bay and garlic; rub over both chickens.
Roast about 2½ hours, until the inner thigh reads 150°. Cool and cut each bird into 10 pieces.
Whisk the buttermilk, hot sauce and sugar, add the chicken, and refrigerate 1 hour.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 375° with the herb sprigs, whole bay leaves and garlic cloves; lift them out once crisp and golden.
Whisk both flours with the garlic and onion powders and the remaining 3 Tbsp salt and 2 Tbsp pepper.
Lift half the chicken from the buttermilk, dredge in the flour and fry over high heat until golden and 160° inside, about 6 minutes for breasts, 8 for other pieces.
Drain, bring the oil back to 375° and fry the rest.
Pile on a platter with the fried herbs and garlic, sprinkle with flaky salt and serve with lemon.

title: Veal Meatballs with Mustard Greens
ingredients: ¼ tsp. chipotle or other smoked chile powder
½ lb. mustard greens, thick stems discarded and leaves chopped
⅓ cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
method: Heat 2 Tbsp oil and cook the onion over moderately high heat about 5 minutes until soft and starting to color.
Add the garlic and all the spices and stir about 2 minutes until aromatic; let cool.
Combine the onion mixture with the veal, breadcrumbs, cream, egg and salt; roll into 1½-inch balls.
Brown the meatballs in the remaining 2 Tbsp oil in a large skillet over moderately high heat, about 5 minutes.
Push them aside, pour off all but 2 Tbsp fat, add the greens and stock, cover and cook about 4 minutes until wilted.
Serve the meatballs and greens in bowls.

title: Radicchio Salad with Manchego Vinaigrette
ingredients: 3 heads of radicchio (2 lbs.)—halved, cored and chopped into 1-inch pieces
method: Soak the chopped onion in the two vinegars at room temperature for 1 hour.
Meanwhile soak the radicchio in ice water for 15 minutes, then drain and dry thoroughly.
Lift out and discard the onion; whisk the honey and olive oil into the flavored vinegar.
Toss the radicchio with the dressing and 1 cup of the Manchego; season with salt and pepper.
Heap on a platter and scatter the remaining ½ cup cheese over the top.

title: Spicy Stir-Fried Cucumbers with Shredded Chicken
ingredients: 12 oz. skinless, boneless chicken breast cutlets, pounded ⅛ inch thick and very thinly sliced crosswise
1 Tbsp. finely chopped peeled fresh ginger
12 dried red chiles, such as chiles de árbol—10 left whole, 2 stemmed and crumbled
1 lb. seedless cucumbers, preferably Persian, cut into 1½-inch pieces
Lemon wedges and steamed rice, for serving
method: Toss the chicken with half the garlic and ginger plus the baking soda, salt and pepper.
Stir the vinegar, sugar and ¼ cup water together in a small bowl.
Heat 2 Tbsp oil in a large skillet until shimmering and stir-fry the chicken over moderately high heat about 2 minutes, until nearly done; set aside.
Add the last 1 Tbsp oil, all the dried chiles, the cucumbers, the vinegar mixture and the rest of the garlic and ginger; season.
Stir-fry over moderate heat about 3 minutes until the cucumbers soften and the liquid mostly cooks off.
Return the chicken with the serrano and cook about 1 minute more until done; stir in cilantro and season.
Serve with lemon wedges and rice.

title: Mixed Citrus & Arugula Salad
ingredients: 1 Tbsp. crème fraîche or sour cream
2 bunches of arugula (¼ lb. each), tough stems discarded
method: Cut away all the peel and white pith from the oranges, tangerines and clementines.
Slice the clementines into ½-inch rounds, removing seeds, and put them in a bowl.
Over the same bowl, cut the orange and tangerine segments free of their membranes. Add the shallot and mint.
Whisk the lime juice, walnut oil and crème fraîche in a large bowl; toss the arugula in it with salt and pepper and plate it.
Toss the citrus in the dressing left in the bowl, season, and arrange over the arugula.

title: Spaghetti with Fresh Asparagus Pesto
ingredients: 1 lb. asparagus, trimmed and coarsely chopped
½ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
¼ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
½ cup basil leaves, torn if large
method: Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente; save ¼ cup of the water before draining.
While it cooks, pulse the raw asparagus in a food processor until finely chopped.
In a large bowl, mix the asparagus with ½ cup oil, the Parmesan, basil and lemon juice; season.
Add the hot pasta and saved water and toss until coated.
Season again, drizzle with more oil and serve.

title: Crispy Tofu Steaks with Ginger Vinaigrette
ingredients: One 14-oz. package firm tofu, drained and sliced 1 inch thick
method: Stir the ginger, scallion, vinegar and ⅓ cup oil together and salt to taste.
Beat the egg in one dish and spread the panko on a plate.
Dip each tofu slice in egg, then press into the panko.
Heat the remaining ⅓ cup oil in a large nonstick skillet and fry the tofu over moderate heat, turning, about 8 minutes until crisp and golden.
Salt the tofu and serve with the ginger dressing.

title: Grilled Cucumbers & Eggplant
ingredients: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
4 Persian or Kirby cucumbers, quartered lengthwise
1 small eggplant, halved lengthwise and cut into wedges
Leaves from 1 small bunch of basil
method: Heat a grill or grill pan.
Whisk ¼ cup oil, the vinegar, garlic and anchovies with salt and pepper.
Coat the cucumbers and eggplant with 3 Tbsp of this dressing.
Oil the grate and grill the vegetables over moderate heat 3 to 5 minutes, turning, until the cucumbers are crisp-tender and the eggplant soft.
Toss the hot vegetables with the remaining dressing and the basil. Serve warm, at room temperature or chilled, with bread.

title: Scallop Carpaccio with Hand-Cut Ginger-Chive Pesto
ingredients: 1 Tbsp. fresh lime juice, plus lime wedges for serving
½ lb. sea scallops, thinly sliced crosswise
Flaky sea salt and thinly sliced radishes, for garnish
method: Mix the ginger, chives, olive oil and lime juice, seasoning with kosher salt and pepper.
Lay the thin scallop slices on a platter.
Spoon the ginger-chive pesto over them.
Finish with flaky salt and radish slices and serve with lime wedges.

title: Crab Salad with Paprika-Scallion Mayonnaise
ingredients: 1 cup finely chopped Vidalia or other sweet onion
⅓ cup plus 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar
¼ cup coarsely chopped flat-leaf parsley
½ small red onion, thinly sliced, for garnish
Buttered toast points or saltines, for serving
method: Layer half the sweet onion in a bowl, add the crab, season, and cover with the rest of the onion.
Whisk the peanut oil, ice water and ⅓ cup vinegar and pour over the crab. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Next day, mix the mayonnaise with the lemon juice, paprika and the last 1 Tbsp vinegar.
Drain the crab and fold it into the mayonnaise with the scallions and parsley.
Top with red onion slices and serve with toast points or crackers.

title: Spicy Fideos with Mussels & Calamari
ingredients: 2 dried chiles de árbol, stemmed and crumbled
7 oz. fideos or angel hair pasta, broken into 1-inch lengths (2 cups)
1 cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
½ lb. cleaned squid, bodies cut into ¼-inch-thick rings and tentacles left whole
method: Mix the parsley and almonds for a topping.
Heat the oil in a wide casserole or paella pan and cook the shallot, garlic, chiles and noodles with salt and pepper over moderately low heat about 5 minutes, until the pasta is toasted.
Add the tomato, tomato paste and saffron and stir about 3 minutes until the paste darkens a little.
Pour in the stock and clam juice, bring to a simmer and cook about 5 minutes until the noodles are al dente.
Stir in the mussels and squid, cover and cook on low 8 to 10 minutes until the mussels open; throw out any that stay shut.
Season and scatter the parsley-almond topping over before serving.

title: Warm Seafood Salad with Pistachios & Capers
ingredients: ½ lb. medium shrimp—shelled, deveined and halved lengthwise
½ lb. cleaned squid, bodies cut into ¼-inch-thick rings and tentacles left whole
method: Pound the anchovies, pistachios, capers, garlic and 1 Tbsp oil in a mortar to a rough paste.
Stir in the remaining 3 Tbsp oil and the lemon juice.
Boil the shrimp in salted water about 20 seconds, just until opaque, and lift into a bowl.
Boil the squid about 20 seconds until just firm, drain and add to the shrimp.
Toss the warm seafood with the pistachio dressing and serve.

title: Cod with Basque Wine Sauce
ingredients: Four 5-oz. skinless cod fillets, halved crosswise
⅓ cup finely chopped flat-leaf parsley
6 oz. shelled and deveined medium shrimp
method: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet until shimmering.
Season the cod and dust it with 1 Tbsp flour; add it to the pan with the garlic and cook over moderately high heat about 2 minutes until just golden.
Sprinkle on the remaining flour, flip the fish, and add the peas, half the parsley, the wine and the cockles.
Cook about 4 minutes, shaking the pan, until the cod is nearly done.
Tuck in the shrimp, cover and cook 2 to 3 minutes until they turn pink and the cockles open; discard any closed ones.
Sprinkle with the rest of the parsley and serve in shallow bowls.

title: Whole Roast Fish with Lemon & Herbs
ingredients: One 2½-lb. whole fish, such as red snapper, cleaned and scaled
¼ cup chopped mixed herbs, such as thyme, oregano, parsley and rosemary
method: Heat the oven to 450° and set the fish on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Cut three crosswise slits to the bone on each side, rub with oil and season with salt and pepper.
Tuck a lemon slice and some herbs into each slit; fill the belly with the shallot, fennel, garlic and the remaining lemon and herbs.
Roast about 20 minutes, until the flesh is opaque.
Meanwhile stir all the salsa verde ingredients together and serve it with the fish.

title: Grape Leaf–Wrapped Salmon with Serrano-Scallion Sauce
ingredients: 16 large jarred grape leaves, drained and patted dry
1 cup orange or yellow grape tomatoes, halved
5 scallions, julienned, plus 2 Tbsp. minced scallion
3 serrano chiles with seeds, halved and thinly sliced
method: Heat the oven to 450° and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
Lay out four overlapping grape leaves per packet. Pile on tomatoes, three-quarters of the julienned scallions and a third of the serranos; season lightly.
Set a seasoned salmon fillet on each pile and fold the leaves around it. Place seam side down on the sheet.
Roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the salmon is medium in the center.
For the sauce, soften the minced scallion in the butter about 2 minutes, add the vinegar and boil about 3 minutes to reduce by half.
Whisk in the cream and simmer about 2 minutes until a little thicker; add the rest of the serranos and season.
Slit open the packets, spoon on the sauce and top with the remaining scallions.

title: Beer-Steamed Shrimp with Cocktail Sauce
ingredients: One 12-oz. can of beer, preferably Pabst Blue Ribbon
method: Snip down the back of each shrimp shell with scissors and pull out the vein, leaving the shell on.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan and cook the onion, garlic, rosemary and chile over moderately high heat 5 to 7 minutes until soft and beginning to brown.
Pour in the beer and simmer about 5 minutes to reduce by half.
Add the lemon halves, Old Bay and 5 cups water and bring just to a simmer.
Add the shrimp and poach gently over low heat 8 to 10 minutes until just cooked; lift everything onto a platter.
Whisk the ketchup, horseradish, lemon juice, Sriracha and Worcestershire for the sauce.
Serve the shrimp warm or at room temperature with the cocktail sauce.

title: Halibut in Parchment with Corn & Tomatoes
ingredients: One 1½-lb. center-cut skinless halibut fillet (1 inch thick)
1 tsp. whole black peppercorns, plus ground pepper for seasoning
4 ears of corn, kernels cut off 3, 1 cob reserved
6 oz. wax or green beans, trimmed (2 cups)
15 small cherry tomatoes (about 8 oz.), preferably on the vine
method: Simmer 1 cup water with the sugar, fennel, peppercorns, coriander and 2½ Tbsp kosher salt until dissolved; off the heat add 3 cups ice water.
Pour the cold brine over the halibut in a shallow dish and leave 25 minutes at room temperature. Pat dry and lightly season one side.
Heat the oven to 400° and lay a 12-by-32-inch sheet of parchment on a baking sheet.
Heap the corn kernels on one half, set the fish on top skinned side up, then add the beans and tomatoes.
Drizzle with oil and vinegar, scatter the herb sprigs, lay the reserved cob alongside and dot the fish with butter.
Fold the paper over, crimp the edges tightly, adding 3 Tbsp water just before sealing.
Roast 20 minutes until the fish is just opaque; open the packet at the table.

title: Potted Ham with Cabbage & Pickles
ingredients: 2 Tbsp. chopped dill, plus more for garnish
method: Warm the anchovies in the olive oil in a small pan over moderate heat, stirring until they dissolve.
Pour the anchovy oil into a bowl and add the ham, cabbage, pickle and chopped dill; season and mix well.
Pack into a 3-cup ramekin and top with more dill.
Serve at room temperature, with toast and mustard if you like.

title: Bacon-Wrapped Vegetable Skewers with Dill Pickle Relish
ingredients: ¾ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
¾ lb. oyster mushrooms, sliced and arranged in 2-inch clusters
20 thin strips of bacon (1 lb.), halved crosswise
method: Mix the pickles, parsley and ¾ cup oil and salt to taste for the relish.
Heat a grill.
Wrap each mushroom cluster and each tomato in a half strip of bacon and thread onto skewers.
Brush with oil, salt lightly and grill over moderate heat about 8 minutes, turning, until the bacon is done and the vegetables soft.
Brush with a little relish in the final minute, then serve with lemon wedges and the rest of the relish.

title: Chile Oil–Marinated Goat Cheese
contributor: Adapted from Les Arcades, Biot, France
ingredients: One 11-oz. log of semifirm goat cheese, cut into 6 pieces
Toasted sliced baguette or sourdough bread, for serving
method: Lay 3 chiles in the bottom of a small bowl at least 3 inches deep.
Set the cheese pieces on top in one layer and add 3 more chiles.
Pour in oil to cover the cheese completely and crumble the last 3 chiles into it.
Cover and refrigerate at least 3 days.
Let come to room temperature and serve with toasted bread for dipping.

title: Pork-Kimchi Dumpling Pancakes
ingredients: ½ Tbsp. gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes) or ½ Tbsp. crushed red pepper
⅓ cup finely chopped drained kimchi
¼ cup firm tofu, finely chopped
method: Stir the sauce ingredients together until the sugar dissolves.
Combine the pork, kimchi, tofu, scallions, garlic, ginger, egg, soy sauce and salt.
Wet the edge of a wrapper, add 1 Tbsp filling, fold into a half-moon and press shut. Repeat, keeping finished dumplings covered.
Mix the cornstarch with 1 cup plus 2 Tbsp water to a thin slurry.
Heat 1 Tbsp oil in an 8-inch nonstick skillet and set 10 dumplings in a tight overlapping ring; fry over moderate heat until browned underneath.
Pour in a third of the slurry, cover for 1 minute, then uncover and cook about 4 minutes until the dumplings are done and a lacy crust forms.
Flip the pancake out onto a plate and repeat twice more. Serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Goat Cheese, Bacon & Olive Quick Bread
time: 35 min active; 1 hr 15 min total, plus cooling
ingredients: 6 slices of thick-cut bacon, cut crosswise into ½-inch-wide strips
½ cup pitted kalamata olives, halved lengthwise
1 red serrano chile, seeded and minced
method: Heat the oven to 350°. Spray a 9-inch loaf pan and line the base with parchment.
Fry the bacon over moderate heat 8 to 10 minutes until crisp; drain.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, cayenne and salt in one bowl and the eggs, buttermilk, oil and mustard in another.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry just until combined.
Fold in both cheeses, the olives, bacon, scallions, chile and thyme, and spread in the pan.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 15 minutes, loosen with a knife, turn out and cool completely before slicing.

title: Roasted Artichokes & Prosciutto
ingredients: 1 lemon, halved, plus 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice
1 Tbsp. very finely chopped flat-leaf parsley
Crusty bread or bread sticks, for serving
method: Heat the oven to 325° and fill a bowl with water acidulated with some of the lemon halves' juice.
Trim each artichoke: pull off dark outer leaves, cut the rest down to 1 inch, peel the base and stem, halve and scoop out the choke.
Quarter, rub with lemon and drop into the lemon water.
In an ovenproof skillet combine the 3 Tbsp lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, thyme and bay leaf; add the drained artichokes and bring to a simmer.
Roast about 40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and spotted brown.
Remove the bay leaf, add parsley, season and let cool.
Serve the artichokes and their oil with the prosciutto and bread.

title: Quick Korean Egg Custards with Shrimp
ingredients: 2 cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
8 small shelled and deveined shrimp (5 oz.)
Toasted sesame seeds and toasted sesame oil, for garnish
method: Whisk the eggs with the stock, fish sauce and salt and divide among four 10-ounce heatproof bowls.
Set the bowls in two wide lidded pots and pour boiling water two-thirds of the way up their sides.
Cover and simmer gently 6 to 7 minutes, until the custards are just a little wobbly in the middle.
Add the shrimp and scallion, cover and steam about 3 minutes more until the shrimp are cooked and the custards set.
Finish with sesame seeds and a few drops of sesame oil; serve warm.

title: Green Pea Samosas (Hare Mutter Ki Samosa)
ingredients: 1 Tbsp. canola oil, plus more for frying
Prepared cilantro chutney and tamarind chutney, for serving
method: Heat 1 Tbsp oil and toast the cumin seeds about 30 seconds; add ginger, jalapeño, coriander and cayenne for another 30 seconds.
Add the peas and ½ cup water and cook about 5 minutes until tender and nearly dry.
Cool slightly in a food processor, add cilantro and pomegranate molasses if using, and pulse to a coarse mash; salt to taste.
Wet the edges of the wrappers and spoon filling onto each.
Shape each into a cone, pinching the seam from the tip, then fold the top down and pinch closed to make a triangle.
Heat ¾ inch of oil to 350° and fry the samosas about 5 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Drain on a rack and serve with both chutneys.

title: Spaghetti with Clams and Braised Greens
ingredients: 1 lb. Swiss chard or collard greens, stemmed and chopped (8 cups)
2 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cubed and chilled
1 tsp. finely grated lemon zest plus 1 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice
½ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, plus more for garnish
method: Heat ¼ cup oil in a big pot and cook half the garlic 1 minute; add the clams and wine and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook over moderately high heat 5 to 7 minutes, pulling clams onto a tray as they open; discard any that stay closed.
Strain the broth into a blender with the roasted peppers and blend smooth.
Rinse the pot, heat the remaining ¼ cup oil and cook the rest of the garlic 1 minute.
Add the pepper flakes and the greens in batches, cooking about 3 minutes until wilted; stir in the pepper broth and season.
Boil the spaghetti until al dente, drain and add to the greens with the butter, lemon zest and juice and ½ cup cheese.
Return the clams, toss to warm through and serve in bowls with more cheese.

title: Spaghetti with Radish-Greens Pesto
ingredients: Greens from 1 big bunch of radishes (8 loosely packed cups), chopped
¾ cup roasted salted pumpkin seeds (3 oz.), plus more for garnish
1 cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, plus more for garnish
method: Pulse the garlic, radish greens, parsley and ¾ cup pumpkin seeds in a food processor until finely chopped.
With the motor running, stream in the olive oil; stir in 1 cup cheese and season.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente, saving 1 cup of the water when you drain.
Put the pasta back in the pot with the pesto, lemon juice and ½ cup of the water.
Toss over low heat about 2 minutes, loosening with more water if needed; season.
Serve topped with extra pumpkin seeds and cheese.

title: Chickpea-Vegetable Stew
ingredients: 1 cup pearl onions—blanched, peeled (or thawed frozen) and halved
½ lb. fingerling potatoes, halved lengthwise
1 Tbsp. finely chopped peeled fresh ginger
3 cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
One 15-oz. can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
method: Heat the oil in a large saucepan and brown the onions and bell pepper over moderately high heat about 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, garlic, ginger and harissa and stir about 2 minutes until the harissa deepens in color.
Pour in the stock and chickpeas, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over moderately low heat 12 to 14 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the coconut milk and return to a simmer.
Stir in lemon juice, season, sprinkle with cilantro and serve with warm flatbread.

title: Cauliflower Steaks with Herb Salsa Verde
ingredients: 1½ Tbsp. capers, drained and coarsely chopped
½ tsp. finely grated lemon zest plus 4½ Tbsp. fresh lemon juice
method: Whisk the parsley, cilantro, tarragon, capers, cornichons, garlic, both mustards and olive oil together.
Slice the cauliflower top to bottom into four ½-inch slabs and season them well.
Get the canola oil very hot in a large skillet and sear the slabs over high heat 2 to 3 minutes until browned.
Flip, pour in the wine and cook 3 to 5 minutes until it evaporates and a knife slides in easily.
Plate the cauliflower and sprinkle with lemon zest.
Stir the lemon juice and vinegar into the herb sauce, season, and spoon it over the steaks.

title: Trout with Preserved Lemon Vinaigrette
method: Whisk the vinegar, lemon juice, preserved lemon, shallot, fish sauce and sugar, then whisk in ¼ cup oil; add parsley and season.
Season the trout. Heat 2 Tbsp oil in a large skillet until shimmering.
Lay in three fillets skin down, pressing them flat, and cook over high heat about 3 minutes until the skin is crisp.
Turn and cook about 30 seconds until just opaque; drain. Wipe the pan and repeat with the remaining oil and fish.
Plate skin side up, top with watercress and spoon some vinaigrette over; pass the rest.

title: Arctic Char with Charmoula
ingredients: ⅓ cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
Four 5-oz. arctic char or salmon fillets with skin
method: Toast the unpeeled garlic in a dry skillet over moderate heat 7 to 8 minutes until the skins blacken; cool and peel.
Blend ⅓ cup oil with the garlic, parsley, cilantro, olives, lemon juice, cumin and paprika until smooth; salt it.
Heat the remaining 2 Tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet and season the fish.
Cook skin side down over moderately high heat about 3 minutes until golden, then flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes until it just flakes.
Drain briefly and serve with the charmoula.

title: Curry Lobster Rolls
ingredients: 8 fresh or frozen kaffir lime leaves
1 Tbsp. vegetable oil, plus more for rubbing
4 hot dog buns or hero rolls, split
method: Heat the oven to 300°. Boil the lobsters about 8 minutes until bright red; drain and cool.
Twist off the tails, cut open the shells and pull out the tail, claw and knuckle meat; split the tails and remove the dark vein. Chill the meat.
Tear each lime leaf off its central stem into two halves, rub with oil and bake about 8 minutes until crisp.
Soften the shallot in 1 Tbsp oil over moderately low heat about 2 minutes, mash in the anchovies, add the curry powder and cook 1 minute.
Cool this mixture, then stir in the mayonnaise, lime juice and dill; salt it and chill 15 minutes.
Fold the curry mayo through the lobster, pile into the buns and top with crisp lime leaves and cucumber.

title: Thai Chicken & Wheat Berry Salad
ingredients: 1 lb. ground chicken, preferably dark meat
½ cup cooked wheat berries or spelt
1 Tbsp. lime juice, plus lime wedges for serving
⅓ cup chopped basil, plus whole leaves for serving
method: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet.
Add the chicken with salt and pepper and cook over moderately high heat, breaking it up, 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through.
Stir in the wheat berries, fish sauce and lime juice.
Take off the heat and mix in the chopped basil.
Serve warm with lettuce cups, lime wedges and basil leaves for wrapping.

title: Chicken Roasted on Bread with Caperberries
ingredients: ½ lb. sourdough bread, torn into bite-size pieces
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
method: Heat the oven to 400°.
On a big rimmed sheet, toss the bread, shallots, caperberries and lemon pieces with ¼ cup oil, salt and pepper.
Brush the chicken legs with oil, season, and set them on top of the bread.
Roast about 50 minutes, until the bread is crisp and the thighs read 160°.
Serve the chicken with the toasted bread and vegetables.

title: Chicken in an Herb Garden
ingredients: 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves (2 lbs.), pounded ¼ inch thick
1 cup finely chopped mixed herbs, such as parsley, tarragon, basil, thyme, rosemary, sage and mint
method: Season the flattened breasts, roll each up tightly lengthwise and pin with toothpicks every inch.
Bring the vinegar, ¾ cup water and a pinch of salt to a gentle simmer.
Poach the rolls over low heat 10 to 12 minutes until just white throughout; cool slightly.
Pull out the toothpicks and cut into 1-inch rounds.
Whisk the olive oil with the herbs, salt and pepper and turn the chicken in it.
Cool 30 minutes, then refrigerate at least 2 hours or overnight.
Bring back to room temperature and serve with bread.

title: Smoked Trout–Caraway Rillettes
ingredients: 3 thinly sliced scallions, plus more for garnish
4 smoked trout fillets (12 oz.), skinned, meat flaked into large pieces
Pickled radishes and rye crackers, for serving
method: Stir together the labneh, shallot, olive oil, caraway and the 3 scallions; season.
Fold in the trout gently so it stays in chunks.
Top with more scallions.
Serve at room temperature with pickled radishes and rye crackers.

title: Potatoes Stuffed with Mushrooms & Fontina
ingredients: 1¼ lbs. mixed tender mushrooms, such as maitake, oyster and enoki, cut into small pieces
½ lb. Italian Fontina cheese, shredded (about 1 cup)
method: Bake the potatoes on a sheet at 450° for 1 hour, until tender.
Meanwhile melt 1 Tbsp butter with the oil and cook the mushrooms over moderately high heat about 5 minutes until golden; season.
Cut each potato open lengthwise halfway down and add 1 Tbsp butter and 2 Tbsp cheese; salt it.
Pile on the mushrooms and the rest of the cheese.
Bake about 3 minutes to melt the cheese, sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.

title: Chicken & Wild Rice Soup
ingredients: 3 celery ribs, cut into ½-inch pieces
2 qts. chicken stock or low-sodium broth
4 cups bite-size pieces of roast chicken or turkey
method: Melt the butter in a large saucepan and cook the celery, carrots, onion, garlic and thyme with salt and pepper over moderate heat about 10 minutes until starting to soften.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir about 3 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the wild rice, then slowly stir in the stock and 2 cups water; bring to a boil.
Simmer over moderately low heat about 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Add the chicken and simmer 10 to 15 minutes more until the rice is tender.
Stir in the cream, season and serve.

title: Ham & Cheese Puff Pastry Tart
ingredients: 3 Tbsp. all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
½ lb. all-butter puff pastry, cut in half
½ lb. thinly sliced baked ham
1 large egg yolk mixed with 1 tsp. water
method: Melt the butter and cook the shallot over moderate heat 3 to 5 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and boil gently 5 to 7 minutes, whisking, until thick.
Add mustard and nutmeg, season and let the sauce cool.
Roll each pastry half to 10 by 6 inches; put one on a parchment-lined sheet.
Leaving a 1-inch border, layer a third of the sauce, half the cheese and half the ham; repeat, then finish with the last of the sauce.
Cover with the second sheet, press and crimp the edges, cut four small slits and brush with egg wash. Chill about 20 minutes.
Bake at 450° for 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

title: Pappardelle with Summer Squash & Arugula-Walnut Pesto
ingredients: ¾ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
½ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, plus shavings for garnish
3 firm, fresh medium zucchini and/or yellow squash (1¼ lbs.), very thinly sliced lengthwise on a mandoline
method: Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over moderately low heat about 5 minutes; chop ½ cup finely and the rest coarsely.
Pulse 2 cups arugula in a food processor until fine and transfer to a big bowl.
Stir in ¾ cup oil, the garlic, grated cheese and finely chopped walnuts; season.
Cook the pappardelle in salted water until al dente, drain and toss with the pesto and squash ribbons.
Add the lemon juice and remaining arugula and season.
Drizzle with oil and top with the coarse walnuts and cheese shavings.

title: Clam & Oyster Pan Roast
ingredients: 2 small leeks, white and tender green parts only, thinly sliced (2 cups)
4 cups chopped mustard or turnip greens
2 dozen oysters, freshly shucked, with their liquor
method: Melt 2 Tbsp butter in a large enameled casserole and cook the leeks with salt over moderate heat about 8 minutes until soft.
Add the greens, thyme, garlic and pepper flakes and stir about 2 minutes until wilted.
Pour in the vermouth, add the clams, boil, then cover and cook 5 to 10 minutes, removing clams as they open; discard any that don't.
Add the oysters with their liquor, the cream, parsley, lemon juice, hot sauce and remaining butter.
Cook 1 to 2 minutes just until the oyster edges curl; remove the thyme.
Return the clams and their juices and serve right away with bread.

title: End-of-Summer Eggplant Bake
ingredients: ½ cup plus 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for greasing
2 spring onions or 6 scallions, thinly sliced
1 tsp. finely grated lemon zest plus 2 tsp. fresh lemon juice
4 oz. country white bread, crusts removed and bread torn into ½-inch pieces (2 cups)
method: Heat the oven to 450°. Spread the eggplant over 2 baking sheets, coat with 6 Tbsp of the oil, season and roast 10 minutes.
Toss the spring onions with 2 Tbsp oil, add them to the eggplant with the butter and roast 15 minutes more, stirring, until tender.
Mix the ricotta with the cream, lemon zest and juice and parsley; season. Toss the bread with the last 1 Tbsp oil.
Spoon the eggplant and onions into a greased 2-quart baking dish, dollop with the ricotta and scatter the bread on top.
Bake about 10 minutes until the bread is golden.
Prep ahead: the roasted eggplant keeps overnight in the fridge; bring to room temperature before finishing.

title: Maryland-Style Crab Cakes
ingredients: 1 tsp. fresh lemon juice, plus wedges for serving
1 lb. jumbo lump crabmeat, picked over for shells
method: Set the broiler to its lowest setting with a rack 12 inches below it; butter a small rimmed baking sheet with 1 Tbsp of the butter.
Whisk the egg with the mayonnaise, lemon juice, salt, pepper and cayenne, then gently fold in the crab and ¼ cup of the breadcrumbs. Chill 10 minutes.
Pack a quarter of the mix into a ½-cup measure, turn it out onto the sheet and shape into a loose patty with damp hands; repeat to make 4.
Scatter the remaining ¼ cup breadcrumbs over the cakes.
Broil 5 minutes until golden, pour the rest of the butter over and broil 1 minute more.
Lift onto plates with a wide spatula and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Grilled Lobsters with Miso-Chile Butter
ingredients: 2 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice, plus wedges for serving
Four 1½-lb. lobsters, halved lengthwise, claws detached and reserved
method: Melt the butter and whisk in the miso, Sriracha and lemon juice; set aside ¼ cup for the table.
Light the grill. Oil and season the scallions, grill about 5 minutes until charred and tender, then chop and toss with 1 Tbsp of the miso butter.
Run a skewer through each lobster half from tail to head so it stays flat; brush the meat with 2 Tbsp miso butter.
Cook the bodies and claws on the grill at moderate heat, turning them and brushing on the rest of the butter: 7 to 8 minutes for tails, 12 to 15 for claws.
Pull out the skewers, pile the lobsters on a platter with the scallions on top and serve with lemon wedges and the reserved butter.

title: Swordfish Skewers with Salsa Verde
ingredients: 1 medium zucchini, very thinly sliced lengthwise on a mandoline
method: Pulse the parsley, garlic, crushed red pepper and oil in a blender to a thick puree; season.
Thread each skewer with alternating bay leaf, swordfish, bay leaf and zucchini ribbon so each ends up with 3 pieces of fish, 3 zucchini slices and 7 bay leaves.
Season the skewers, brush all over with the parsley sauce and refrigerate 1 hour.
Grill over moderate heat, turning, about 6 minutes until the fish is browned and cooked through.
Grill the lemon halves cut side down about 2 minutes until charred.
Serve the skewers with the grilled lemons, discarding the bay leaves.

title: Steamed Bass with Spicy Butter
ingredients: Four 7-oz. sea bass or red snapper fillets with skin
One 1½-inch piece of fresh ginger, peeled and cut into very thin matchsticks
Finely grated zest and juice of 1 lime
4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
Chopped cilantro leaves and sliced scallion, for garnish
method: Slash the skin of each fillet 4 times and lay them skin side up in a large glass or ceramic pie plate.
Scatter over the ginger, chile, garlic and lime zest, season, dot with the butter and pour on the lime juice.
Put 3 balls of foil in a very large deep skillet, add 1 inch of water and bring to a boil.
Rest the pie plate on the foil, cover tightly and steam about 5 minutes until the fish flakes.
Move the fillets to shallow bowls, spoon over the buttery juices and top with cilantro and scallion.

title: Easy Persian Fried Fish
ingredients: Four 6-oz. red snapper (or other white fish) fillets with skin
Lemon wedges and greens, for serving
method: Stir the dried herbs, cayenne and turmeric into the flour in a shallow bowl.
Season the fillets and coat them in the spiced flour.
Heat the oil in a large cast-iron skillet until shimmering.
Lay the fish in skin side down, press flat with a spatula and cook over moderately high heat about 4 minutes until the skin browns.
Flip and cook about 2 minutes more until opaque throughout; serve with lemon wedges and greens.

title: Turkey Tonnato
ingredients: 1 lb. thinly sliced roast turkey breast
One 6½-oz. can tuna in water, drained
½ cup chopped mixed herbs, such as tarragon, chives and dill
method: Lay the turkey slices out on a platter.
Blend the tuna, chickpeas and yogurt in a food processor.
With the motor running, pour in the oil until the sauce is smooth.
Add the capers and chopped herbs, then season.
Spoon the sauce over the turkey and serve.

title: Ham Glazed with Cider & Cloves
method: Heat the oven to 375° and set the ham in a 9-by-13-inch baking dish.
Simmer everything else together in a small saucepan over moderately low heat about 25 minutes, until reduced to ¾ cup.
Pour the glaze over the ham, spices and all, cover tightly with foil and bake about 1 hour 15 minutes, basting every 15 minutes, until hot through.
Move the ham to a platter and strain the pan juices into a small saucepan.
Boil the juices 8 to 10 minutes to a glaze and spoon over the ham.
Prep ahead: the glaze can be made 2 days in advance and refrigerated; rewarm before using.

title: Pan-Roasted Chicken with Tarragon Crème Fraîche
ingredients: 1 tsp. dried summer savory or dried oregano
2 medium carrots, sliced diagonally 1 inch thick
¼ head of cauliflower, cut into 1½-inch florets
¼ lb. haricots verts or thin green beans
4 boneless chicken breast halves with skin
¼ cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
method: Grind the coriander, mustard seeds, peppercorns and savory to a powder.

Steam the vegetables in layers (potatoes, carrots, cauliflower, beans) over 1 inch of simmering water, lifting out the beans after about 3 minutes, the cauliflower 3 minutes later and the carrots and potatoes after 10 minutes more.
Toss the vegetables in 2 Tbsp butter over moderately high heat about 1 minute, add the lemon juice and season.

Season the chicken and coat with the ground spices. Cook skin side down in the remaining 3 Tbsp butter over moderately low heat about 12 minutes until deeply browned, then turn and cook, basting, about 7 minutes more.
Rewarm the vegetables. Boil the stock in the chicken skillet 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, then boil in the crème fraîche, take off the heat and stir in the tarragon; season.
Sauce the chicken and serve with the vegetables alongside.
Prep ahead: the spice mix and steamed vegetables can be done a day in advance.

title: Roast Chicken with Salsa Verde & Roasted Lemons
ingredients: One 4-lb. chicken, backbone removed, chicken halved lengthwise
1 cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
method: Heat the oven to 450°. Set the chicken halves skin side up on a rack over a baking sheet, rub with 2 Tbsp oil and season.
Put the lemon halves cut side down on the rack and roast about 40 minutes until the chicken is golden and cooked through; rest 10 minutes.
Meanwhile pound the capers, anchovies and garlic to a paste in a mortar or blender.
Whisk the remaining 1 cup oil into the paste, stir in all the herbs and salt to taste.
Carve the chicken, arrange with the roasted lemons and serve with the salsa verde (it can be made the night before and served at room temperature).

title: Coconut Rice Bowl with Chicken
method: Bring the rice, coconut milk, sugar and ½ tsp salt to a boil in a large saucepan.
Cover and cook over low heat about 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed.
Let the rice stand off the heat for 10 minutes.
Tip into a bowl and fold through the chicken, cucumber and oil.
Season with salt, top with scallions and serve.

title: Sweet & Sticky Hot Wings
ingredients: 2½ Tbsp. red hot sauce, preferably Frank's RedHot
method: Heat the oven to 500° and line a large baking sheet with foil coated in cooking spray.
Mix the flour, salt, paprika, dried garlic and onion in a large bowl and toss the wings through it.
Spread the wings on the sheet, mist with spray and roast 45 minutes, turning once or twice, until crisp and browned.
Whisk the hot sauce with the melted butter and pepper jelly in a large bowl.
Toss the hot wings in the glaze and serve.

title: Bacon & Egg Pizza
ingredients: 6 oz. thick-sliced bacon, cut crosswise into ⅓-inch lardons
3 oz. Brie, thinly sliced (with rind, if desired)
method: Put a pizza stone in the oven and heat to 500°. Bake the bacon in a pie plate 15 minutes, stirring once, until almost crisp; drain.

Beat the eggs with the cream and a little salt, then cook with 1 Tbsp butter in a nonstick skillet over low heat, whisking often, about 12 minutes to a creamy small curd. Off the heat stir in the other 1 Tbsp butter and salt.
Stretch the dough to a 12-inch round on a floured peel, spread with crème fraîche leaving a 1-inch rim, and top with the bacon, Brie and mozzarella.
Bake on the stone about 7 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Spoon the scrambled eggs over, return to the stone about 2 minutes until hot, scatter with chives and cut into wedges.

title: Moo Shu Shrimp
ingredients: ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil
1 lb. shelled and deveined medium shrimp
3 oz. sliced mixed wild mushrooms (1 packed cup)
3 scallions, halved lengthwise and cut into 1-inch lengths
1 Tbsp. hoisin sauce, plus more for serving
method: Warm the tortillas wrapped in foil in a 200° oven.
Get a wok very hot, add 1 Tbsp oil until smoking and stir-fry the shrimp about 2 minutes until just cooked; move to a platter.
Add 2 Tbsp oil, pour in the seasoned eggs and stir about 2 minutes to soft curds; add to the shrimp.
Stir-fry the ginger, garlic and mushrooms in 2 Tbsp oil about 4 minutes until browned.
Add the last 1 Tbsp oil with the coleslaw mix and scallions, season and stir-fry about 4 minutes until the cabbage just wilts.
Return the shrimp and eggs, toss with 1 Tbsp hoisin and serve with the tortillas, cilantro and extra hoisin.

title: Spring Rolls with Pork & Glass Noodles
ingredients: ½ cup finely shredded green cabbage
½ cup thinly sliced yellow onion (½ small)
½ cup julienned taro or potato
Chinese hot mustard and/or sweet chile sauce, for dipping
method: Boil the noodles 4 to 5 minutes until al dente, chill in ice water, drain and cut into 3-inch lengths.
Combine the noodles with the pork, carrots, cabbage, onion, taro, oyster sauce, salt, sugar and pepper.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a large casserole to 350°.
Set a wrapper with a corner toward you, put ¼ cup filling in the lower third, roll up tucking in the sides and seal the tip with beaten egg; repeat, keeping the wrappers under a damp towel.
Fry the rolls about 5 minutes, turning, until golden and the pork is cooked; drain on paper towels.
Serve with hot mustard and/or sweet chile sauce. Unfried rolls can be refrigerated up to 4 hours under a damp cloth.

title: Drunken Noodles
ingredients: 7 oz. firm tofu, cubed and dried
½ cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
1 tsp. black soy sauce or ¾ tsp. soy sauce sweetened with ¼ tsp. molasses
½ red bell pepper, seeded and sliced
½ large jalapeño, seeded and sliced
½ lb. pad thai rice noodles, cooked and cut in half crosswise
1 cup Thai basil leaves, plus more for garnish
method: Fry the tofu in ¼ inch of oil over moderately high heat about 5 minutes, turning, until crisp; drain.
Stir the stock with the oyster, fish and soy sauces, the chile paste and the sugar.
Stir-fry the bell pepper, jalapeño, garlic and Thai chile in 2 Tbsp oil over high heat about 2 minutes.
Add the noodles and stir-fry about 4 minutes until browned.
Add the sauce and keep tossing over moderately high heat until it is soaked up, then mix in the basil and tofu.
Top with extra basil leaves and put lime wedges alongside.

title: Vermicelli with Chicken Skewers & Nuoc Cham
ingredients: 5 Tbsp. Asian fish sauce (nuoc mam or nam pla)
1 lb. skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, cut lengthwise into 12 strips
12 long wooden skewers, soaked in water for 1 hour
2 Tbsp. plus 1 tsp. fresh lime juice (from about 2 limes)
1 cucumber—peeled, halved lengthwise, seeded and thinly sliced
⅔ cup mint, basil or cilantro leaves, or any combination of these
method: Heat the broiler or grill. Toss the chicken strips with 1 Tbsp fish sauce, 1 Tbsp sugar, 2 of the garlic cloves and the oil, thread onto skewers and cook about 2 minutes per side.
For the nuoc cham, mix the other 4 Tbsp fish sauce, 1 Tbsp sugar and last garlic clove with the chile flakes, vinegar, lime juice and 2 Tbsp water.
Boil the vermicelli in salted water about 9 minutes, adding the bean sprouts for the final minute; drain, rinse cold and drain well.
Spread the noodles and sprouts on a platter and top with cucumber, herbs and the skewers.
Pour over the nuoc cham, scatter with peanuts and serve.

title: Honey-Ginger Chicken with Lime
ingredients: ⅓ cup minced peeled fresh ginger
4 chicken legs, cut into drumsticks and thighs
method: Heat the oven to 400°. Make a marinade of the vinegar, honey, ginger, jalapeño, all the spices, salt, pepper and 3 tsp of the lime zest.
Prick the chicken all over with a fork and toss it in the marinade. Mix the sugar with the remaining ½ tsp zest.
Brown the chicken in 2 Tbsp butter and the oil in a large ovenproof skillet over moderately high heat about 5 minutes, turning.
Sprinkle with the lime sugar and roast 25 minutes until cooked through.
Stir the lime juice and remaining 2 Tbsp butter into the pan juices and serve with lime wedges, plus rice or naan.

title: Coq au Riesling
ingredients: 1½ cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
method: Heat the oven to 300°. Season the chicken and brown it in two batches in 2 Tbsp canola oil, about 8 minutes a batch; pour off the fat and wipe the pot.
Soften the onion, carrot, celery and shallots in the remaining 2 Tbsp oil about 8 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the Riesling, simmer 1 minute scraping the pot, then pour in the stock, add the thyme and bring up to a boil.
Tuck in the chicken, cover and braise in the oven 1 hour until tender.
Meanwhile brown the mushrooms in the butter and olive oil over high heat about 5 minutes without stirring, then season and cook 3 to 5 minutes more.
Lift out the chicken, strain and skim the braising liquid and boil it down to 1½ cups; whisk in the crème fraîche and lemon juice and season.
Return the chicken and mushrooms to the sauce, simmer 3 minutes and finish with tarragon.

title: Turkey Curry Soup
ingredients: ½ small kabocha squash (1 lb.)—peeled, seeded and cut into 1½-inch pieces (4 cups)
½ cup chopped mixed herbs, such as cilantro and basil
method: Heat the oil in a large saucepan and fry the curry paste with the squash over high heat about 3 minutes until lightly caramelized.
Add 4 cups water with the coconut milk and fish sauce and bring up to a boil.
Cover and simmer about 15 minutes until the squash is tender.
Finish with the turkey, lime juice and herbs, check the seasoning and serve.

title: Sichuan-Style Green Beans with Pork
ingredients: ¾ lb. green beans, thinly sliced crosswise
7 to 10 dried Chinese hot red chiles, cracked
method: Heat the oil in a large skillet until shimmering.
Brown the pork over moderately high heat, breaking it up, about 5 minutes until nearly done.
Add the green beans, chiles and garlic and stir-fry over high heat about 7 minutes until the beans are crisp-tender.
Season with the soy sauce, lime juice, salt and white pepper.
Serve over steamed rice.

title: Ham & Gruyère French Toast Sandwiches
ingredients: 2 Granny Smith apples—peeled, cored and thinly sliced
Eight ½-inch-thick hand-cut slices from a loaf of white bread
½ lb. thickly sliced smoked ham
method: Simmer the apples with the maple syrup, cinnamon stick and 1 cup water about 6 minutes until tender; lift out and cool.
Whisk the milk and eggs in a shallow bowl. Spread 4 bread slices with mustard and layer on half the cheese, the ham and the rest of the cheese.
Melt 1 Tbsp butter in a large skillet over low heat. Dip the bottoms of the topped slices in the egg and set them in the pan; dip the lids on one side only and put them soaked side up.
Cover and cook over moderately low heat about 3 minutes until browned underneath, flip (adding butter if needed), cover and cook about 3 minutes more until the cheese melts.
Rest 5 minutes, halve and serve with the maple apples and some steamed greens.

title: Sausage Choucroute
ingredients: 1 lb. mixed sausages, such as bratwurst and fresh chorizo
1 lb. small Yukon Gold potatoes, quartered
One 25-oz. jar of sauerkraut, drained (3 cups)
Crusty bread and grainy mustard, for serving
method: Heat the oven to 425°.
Toss the sausages, potatoes, sauerkraut, oil and caraway in a large cast-iron skillet and season.
Roast about 45 minutes until the potatoes are golden and cooked through.
Serve with crusty bread and grainy mustard.

title: Sweet & Sour Pork in Lettuce Cups
ingredients: 1 tsp. finely grated lime zest plus 2 Tbsp. fresh lime juice
1 head of butter lettuce (6 oz.), leaves separated
method: Soften the onion in the oil over moderate heat about 5 minutes until golden, then cook the garlic 1 minute.
Add the pork and brown about 3 minutes, breaking it up.
Season with the honey, fish sauce and sesame oil and give it 2 more minutes until the pork is fully cooked.
Off the heat add the lime zest and juice and season.
Spoon into lettuce leaves, top with scallions and serve with lime wedges.

title: Thai-Style Pulled Pork Sandwiches
ingredients: ⅓ cup Thai red curry paste
¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. finely grated palm sugar or dark brown sugar
One 4-lb. boneless pork shoulder roast with fat cap
1 stalk of fresh lemongrass, inner light green and white parts only, cut into 3 pieces
One ½-inch piece of fresh ginger, peeled and thinly sliced
One 15-oz. can unsweetened coconut milk, chilled
⅓ cup chicken stock or low-sodium broth
½ cup each finely chopped cilantro, Thai basil and mint leaves
Thinly sliced cucumber and red onion, cilantro, Thai basil and lime wedges, for serving
method: Heat the oven to 325°. Warm the curry paste, fish sauce and ¼ cup of palm sugar together, stirring, until smooth; cool a little.
Salt the pork, rub it with the paste, and roast covered in a large casserole about 3½ hours until very tender, basting now and then; uncover for the last 15 minutes to crust.
Rest 15 minutes, shred with forks and stir the skimmed pan juices back through; keep warm.

Seal the cilantro stems and all the remaining aromatics and spices (garlic through turmeric) in a double foil packet and set it on a burner or hot cast-iron pan about 5 minutes until smoky and lightly charred inside.
Process the packet contents with the remaining 2 Tbsp palm sugar to a paste.
Simmer the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk, whisk in the paste, then the rest of the coconut milk and the stock.
Stir in the pork, season and simmer about 10 minutes to thicken; add the chopped herbs.
Pile onto mayonnaise-spread buns with cucumber, red onion, cilantro and basil and serve with lime wedges.

title: Watermelon, Feta & Charred Pepper Salad
ingredients: 1 lb. seedless watermelon, cut into 1-inch cubes (from one 3¼-lb. watermelon)
2 Kirby cucumbers, peeled and cut into ¾-inch dice
¼ cup very thinly sliced red onion
½ tsp. gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes) or Aleppo pepper
¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
method: In a large baking dish gently combine the watermelon, cucumbers, onion, vinegar, gochugaru and ¼ cup of the oil; spread out and season.
Sear the shishitos in the remaining 2 Tbsp oil over high heat about 2 minutes until blistered and crisp-tender.
Toss the peppers through the watermelon.
Plate and finish with the olives, feta, watercress, cilantro and dill; eat straight away.
wines: Warm-climate rosé from Australia or South America

title: Marinated Olives with Orange
method: Warm the oil in a large skillet and cook the garlic, orange zest and crushed red pepper over moderate heat about 2 minutes until the garlic softens.
Add the olives and heat through about 5 minutes, stirring.
Take off the heat and stir in the orange juice.
Cool completely, stirring occasionally, and serve at room temperature.

title: Soft-Scrambled Eggs with Smoked Sablefish & Trout Roe
ingredients: ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. heavy cream
4 oz. smoked sablefish, sliced ¼ inch thick
Trout roe, thinly sliced scallions and sour cream, for garnish
Toasted sesame, everything or plain bagels, for serving
method: Put the eggs, cream and ½ Tbsp of the butter in a medium nonstick skillet.
Cook over moderately low heat, whisking constantly, 5 to 7 minutes until small creamy curds form; remove from the heat.
Fold in the remaining ½ Tbsp butter and a little salt.
Divide between 2 bowls, lay the sablefish on top and garnish with trout roe, scallions and sour cream.
Serve at once with toasted bagels (smoked salmon and salmon roe can stand in).

title: Ham, Leek & Gouda Soufflés
ingredients: 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, plus softened butter for brushing
¼ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
2 leeks, white parts only, thinly sliced
¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. all-purpose flour
method: Heat the oven to 400°. Butter eight 1-cup ramekins, dust with 2 Tbsp of the Parmigiano and set on a sturdy baking sheet.
Wilt the leeks in 2 Tbsp butter over high heat about 5 minutes; set aside and wipe the pan.
Make a thick white sauce: melt the remaining 4 Tbsp butter, cook the flour 1 minute, whisk in the milk and cook about 2 minutes until very thick; add the salt and cayenne.
Off the heat whisk in the yolks, cool slightly, then stir in the Gouda, ham and leeks in a large bowl.
Beat the whites with the cream of tartar to firm peaks and fold into the base until no streaks remain.

Fill the ramekins to ½ inch below the rim, run a thumb round the inside edge, top with the last 2 Tbsp Parmigiano and bake in the lower third of the oven 20 minutes until puffed and golden; serve at once.
Variation: bake in one 8-cup soufflé dish at 375° for 40 minutes. The yolk base can be made the night before.

title: Ratatouille Toasts with Fried Eggs
ingredients: ¾ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
3 medium tomatoes, seeded and cut into ½-inch dice (2 cups)
One 12-oz. eggplant, seeds removed and flesh cut into ½-inch dice (2 cups)
2 small zucchini, cut into ½-inch dice (2 cups)
2 large red onions, cut into ½-inch dice
1 red bell pepper, cut into ½-inch dice
1 cup chopped basil, plus more for garnish
Six ½-inch-thick slices of sourdough bread, toasted
method: Cook the tomatoes in 2 Tbsp oil with 1 garlic clove, ¼ tsp crushed red pepper and salt over moderate heat about 5 minutes until just soft; tip into a saucepan, discarding the garlic.

Cook the eggplant, zucchini, onions and bell pepper the same way, one vegetable at a time, each with 2 Tbsp oil, a garlic clove, ¼ tsp crushed red pepper and salt, about 7 minutes each, adding each to the saucepan.
Add the bay leaf, ½ cup basil and ⅓ cup water, cover and cook over moderately low heat about 20 minutes until very tender.
Discard the bay leaf, stir in the remaining ½ cup basil, season and cool a little.
Fry the eggs in the last 2 Tbsp oil in two batches of 3, 3 to 5 minutes, until the whites set and the yolks stay runny; season.
Spoon ratatouille onto the toasts, top each with an egg, and finish with a drizzle of oil and basil. The ratatouille keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Sun-Dried Tomato & Arugula Pizza
ingredients: 4 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for greasing
method: Mix the flour, sugar and yeast in a stand mixer with the dough hook, then work in half the warm water, the 3 Tbsp oil and the salt, followed by the rest of the water, until a ball forms; knead 2 minutes low, 2 medium, 2 low.
Rise the dough in an oiled, covered bowl about 1½ hours until doubled.
Heat a pizza stone on the oven floor at 500° for about 45 minutes.
Punch down the dough, divide into 8 balls, flatten into disks and rest covered 20 minutes.
Simmer the sun-dried tomatoes in water about 5 minutes until soft, drain and chop; puree the garlic with the ⅓ cup oil.
Roll or stretch a disk to an 8-inch round on a floured peel, brush with garlic oil, scatter with an eighth of the tomatoes and cheese, drizzle with more garlic oil and season.
Bake on the stone about 4 minutes until crisp and bubbling, top with arugula and serve; repeat with the rest.
Prep ahead: the punched-down dough, tomatoes and garlic oil can all be refrigerated overnight.

title: Roast Dorade with Figs, Olives & Almonds
ingredients: Four 12-oz. dorade—scaled, cleaned and patted dry
5 dried Turkish figs, stemmed and quartered
½ cup each pitted Cerignola and Castelvetrano olives
method: Heat the oven to 350° and slick a large roasting pan with 1 Tbsp of the oil.
Lay in the dorade and salt them well.
Strew the figs, olives, rosemary and almonds around and over the fish, then pour on the wine and the remaining 3 Tbsp oil.
Roast about 30 minutes until the flesh just flakes and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Tuna Niçoise Burgers
ingredients: 1 Tbsp. salted capers, rinsed and minced
Sliced tomatoes and arugula, for serving
method: Spread the tuna, scallion, olive and caper mixture on a plate and firm it up in the freezer 5 minutes.
Pulse the mixture in a food processor until finely chopped, season and shape into four 4-inch patties.
Brush the burgers with oil and grill over moderately high heat about 6 minutes, turning once, until crusty and just cooked through.
Stir the anchovy paste into the mayonnaise and spread on the buns.
Add the burgers, tomato and arugula and serve.

title: Provençal Tuna Sandwiches with Fennel Mayo
ingredients: 1 medium fennel bulb, shaved paper-thin, plus 2 Tbsp. chopped fronds
1 Tbsp. finely grated lemon zest plus 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice
¼ cup finely chopped red onion
¼ cup pitted niçoise olives, chopped
Two 6-oz. jars tuna packed in olive oil, drained and flaked
method: Toast the fennel seeds about 3 minutes until golden and crush them in a mortar.
Puree the crushed seeds into the mayonnaise and crème fraîche with the garlic, fennel fronds, 2 tsp zest and 1 Tbsp lemon juice; season.
Mix the onion with the olives, capers, chile flakes and the remaining zest and juice, then fold in the tuna and olive oil.
Spread the fennel mayo over both cut sides of the baguette.
Layer arugula, shaved fennel and the tuna on the base, then tomatoes, cucumber and anchovies.
Close, cut into 4 and serve; wrapped in parchment the sandwiches keep 4 hours in the fridge, the mayo 3 days.

title: Smoky Paella with Shrimp & Squid
ingredients: 1 lb. large shrimp, shelled and deveined
½ lb. baby squid, bodies cut into ¼-inch rings
method: Sear the seasoned shrimp on one side in the hot oil in a large deep skillet about 2 minutes; set aside.
Toast the rice in the skillet about 2 minutes until opaque, then stir in the tomato paste, paprika, garlic and saffron for 1 minute.
Add the clam juice and 2 cups water, bring to a boil and boil about 10 minutes until half the liquid is absorbed.
Lower the heat and simmer about 8 minutes until the rice is nearly tender and still soupy.
Stir in the squid, lay the shrimp on top cooked side up, cover and simmer about 2 minutes more until everything is cooked through.

title: Octopus with Chorizo & Potatoes
ingredients: ¾ lb. potatoes, peeled and cut into ½-inch dice
3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
5 oz. cured Spanish chorizo, cut into ½-inch dice
method: Boil a large pan of salted water with the onion and bay leaves; dip the octopus in 3 times, then leave it to cook over moderately low heat about 1 hour until tender.
Rest the octopus in the water 10 minutes off the heat, drain and cut into ½-inch pieces.
Boil the potatoes in salted water about 10 minutes until just tender, drain and toss with the 3 Tbsp oil and thyme; season.
Warm the chorizo in a grill pan about 2 minutes and move to a large bowl.
Cook the potatoes and octopus in the same pan about 5 minutes until hot and golden in spots.
Toss with the chorizo, season, drizzle with oil and add shiso if you like.

title: Salmon & Cherry Tomato Skewers with Rosemary Vinaigrette
ingredients: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
1½ lbs. skinless salmon fillet, cut into 1½-inch cubes
4 long metal skewers, or 4 wooden skewers soaked in water for 1 hour
method: Whisk the ¼ cup oil with the lemon juice, mustard and rosemary and season the vinaigrette.
Heat a grill or grill pan and thread the salmon and tomatoes onto the skewers.
Brush with oil, season all over and grill over moderately high heat about 6 minutes, turning once, until the salmon is just cooked.
Drizzle the skewers with some vinaigrette and pass the rest at the table.

title: Chicken with Piquillos
method: Rub the chicken pieces with the garlic and 1 Tbsp salt and refrigerate, covered, for 1 hour.
Scrape off the garlic and brown the chicken in the oil in a large deep skillet over moderately high heat about 12 minutes; set aside.
Cook the onion in the pan over low heat about 10 minutes until very soft.
Add the piquillos and wine and bring to a simmer, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the chicken with its juices, partly cover and cook over low heat about 30 minutes until tender and the sauce has thickened.
Spoon the sauce over the chicken to serve; it reheats well the next day.

title: Smoked-Duck Salad with Walnuts & Raspberries
ingredients: ½ lb. smoked duck breast—skin and fat removed and reserved, breast thinly sliced crosswise
6 oz. frisée, torn into bite-size pieces (6 cups)
method: Heat the oven to 350°. Bake the reserved duck skin and fat in a pie plate about 15 minutes until crisp; drain and break into cracklings.
Toast the walnuts in the oven about 8 minutes, cool and chop coarsely.
Whisk the vinegar, mustard and shallot, then slowly whisk in the walnut and vegetable oils; season well.
Toss the frisée, Boston lettuce and walnuts in the dressing.
Top with raspberries, sliced duck and cracklings and serve.

title: Sausages with Peaches & Pickled Chiles
ingredients: 2 medium peaches, pitted and sliced ¼ inch thick
method: Shake both vinegars with the sorghum, salt and ½ cup water in a jar until the salt dissolves.
Add the jalapeños and onion and leave at room temperature at least 1 hour.
Grill the sausages over moderate heat on an oiled grate, turning, 10 to 12 minutes until charred and cooked through.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly on the diagonal.
Lay the peach slices on a platter, pile on the sausages and some pickles, drizzle with pickling liquid and pass the rest of the pickles.

title: Spaghetti with Mushroom Bolognese
ingredients: ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
1 small onion, cut into ¼-inch dice
2 medium carrots, peeled and cut into ¼-inch dice
1 baby eggplant (8 oz.), peeled and cut into ¼-inch dice
1 lb. cremini mushrooms, one-fourth sliced, the rest cut into ¼-inch dice
8 oz. shiitake mushrooms, stemmed, caps cut into ¼-inch dice
One 2-inch chunk of Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, plus grated cheese for serving
One 28-oz. can whole peeled tomatoes, crushed
method: Soak the porcini in 1 cup boiling water about 30 minutes; chop finely and keep ½ cup of the liquid.
Cook the onion and carrots in 2 Tbsp oil in a large casserole about 8 minutes until light golden, then add the eggplant with 2 Tbsp more oil and cook 8 minutes.
Add all the mushrooms and the last 2 Tbsp oil, season, and cook 8 to 10 minutes until golden.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and miso for 2 minutes, then add the cheese chunk, tomatoes, thyme, sugar and soaking liquid.
Cover and simmer over low heat about 1½ hours until very thick; discard the thyme and season.
Boil the spaghetti until al dente, keeping ¼ cup of the water.
Toss the pasta, water and parsley with the sauce and serve with grated cheese.

title: Leek & Mushroom Croquettes
ingredients: 2 leeks, white and tender green parts only, thinly sliced
¼ lb. shiitake mushrooms, stemmed, caps thinly sliced
3 Tbsp. all-purpose flour, plus more for coating
¼ cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
2 large eggs beaten with 2 Tbsp. water
method: Cook the leeks and shiitake in 2 Tbsp butter over high heat about 7 minutes until soft and browning; season, add the herbs and tip into a bowl.
Make a thick white sauce with the remaining 3 Tbsp butter, 3 Tbsp flour and the milk, cooking about 3 minutes; stir it into the vegetables with both cheeses and season.
Spoon the mixture onto plastic wrap, roll into a 14-inch log and freeze about 2 hours until firm.
Cut the log into 12 pieces and pat each into a 2-inch patty with floured hands.
Coat each in flour, egg and panko, then freeze 15 minutes.
Fry in ½ inch of 375° oil about 5 minutes, turning, until golden; drain and serve hot.

title: Carrot Osso Buco
ingredients: 3 very large carrots, cut crosswise 1 inch thick at the wide ends and 1½ inches thick toward the narrow ends
1 Tbsp. porcini mushroom powder (ground dried porcini mushrooms)
method: Heat the oven to 350°. Blanch the pearl onions 1 minute in a deep ovenproof skillet, then trim and peel them.
Brown the carrot pieces in 1 Tbsp oil over moderate heat, seasoned, about 5 minutes a side.
Add the onions and curry powder for 1 minute, pour in the wine and simmer 3 minutes.
Add the porcini powder and broth, bring to a boil and braise in the oven 1 hour 15 minutes, turning once, until tender.
Season the sauce and spoon carrots, onions and sauce into bowls.
Toss the parsley with lemon juice and the last 1 tsp oil, season and scatter over. Good with soft polenta or celery root puree.

title: Crusty Baked Shells & Cauliflower
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
¾ lb. medium shells, such as Barilla
2½ lbs. cauliflower, cut into small florets (1 large head)
3 Tbsp. roughly chopped fresh sage leaves
¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes
2 cups freshly grated Italian Fontina Val d'Aosta cheese, lightly packed (10 oz. with rind)
6 Tbsp. freshly grated Italian Pecorino cheese
method: Heat the oven to 400°. Boil the shells in well-salted water just to al dente, drain and put in a very large bowl.
Sauté the cauliflower in two batches in 3 Tbsp olive oil each over medium-high heat, 5 to 6 minutes per batch, until browned and tender; add to the pasta.
Stir in the sage, capers, garlic, lemon zest, pepper flakes, 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp pepper, then the Fontina.
Spread half the mixture in a 10 x 13-inch baking dish, dot with spoonfuls of ricotta and cover with the rest.
Mix the panko, Pecorino, parsley and 1 Tbsp oil and scatter on top.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until browned and crusty. Can be assembled a day ahead and baked before serving.

title: Lentil & Smoky Eggplant Stew
ingredients: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
3 cups French green du Puy lentils (20 oz.), rinsed and picked over
Greek yogurt, chopped walnuts and parsley, small mint leaves and pomegranate molasses, for serving
method: Soften the onion, celery, garlic and bay leaf in 2 Tbsp oil over moderate heat.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and stock, cover and simmer about 45 minutes until the lentils are tender but intact; remove the bay leaf.
Meanwhile rub the eggplants with the remaining oil and broil 6 inches from the heat about 20 minutes, turning, until blackened and soft.
Halve the eggplants, scoop the flesh into a colander to drain 5 minutes, then mash smooth.
Stir the harissa and half the eggplant into the lentils, add the parsley and season.
Serve topped with the rest of the eggplant, yogurt, walnuts, parsley, mint, pomegranate molasses and a drizzle of oil.

title: Poulet Basquaise with Currant Couscous
time: 1 hr 15 min active; 2 hr 30 min total
ingredients: 6 whole chicken legs, separated into thighs and drumsticks
¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
method: Heat the oven to 350°. Season the chicken and brown it in the oil in a large casserole in two batches, about 8 minutes each; set aside.
Leaving 2 Tbsp fat, cook the onion, poblano and bell pepper 8 to 10 minutes until soft, then the tomatoes about 8 minutes until broken down.
Add the pimentón for 1 minute, then the wine, vinegar, thyme and bay leaves and reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Tuck in the chicken, cover and braise in the oven about 1 hour 15 minutes; discard the thyme and bay leaves.
For the couscous, boil the wine, oil, saffron and 1 cup water and pour over the couscous, currants, onion and salt in a bowl.
Cover and leave about 30 minutes until absorbed, fluff and serve with the chicken.

title: Chicken Legs Coq au Vin
ingredients: 2 thyme sprigs, plus chopped thyme for garnish
method: Season the drumsticks, dust with 2 Tbsp flour and brown in the oil in a large casserole about 5 minutes; set aside.
Crisp the bacon, then cook the carrot, onion, celery, mushrooms and garlic about 5 minutes until golden.
